ST-19.title: Structural fix for recurring cross-EPIC execution_state.json merge-conflict pattern

process_notes: Commit 8d5411b2fdd39b7ee3f99a63982a948e14a8a965 (message '[EPIC-04][ST-15][ST-16][ST-17] ...') also modified ST-13 and ST-14's execution_state.json fields (delegation_record_id, status transition in_progress/not_started -> blocked_backend) without including ST-13/ST-14 in the commit message, violating CLAUDE.md's commit-format rule (all story IDs touched by a commit must appear in the message). Self-caught after push; not amended (commit already pushed - amending a pushed commit is avoided per repo convention). No functional impact: neither ST-13 nor ST-14 reached a 'done'/closed-issue state in this commit, so governance_sync.yml's auto-close behavior was not affected. Recorded here for QA evidence log completeness at EPIC-04 close.

Structural gotcha discovered this EPIC (candidate lessons-learnt item): governance_sync.yml auto-closes a GitHub issue whenever a commit message contains that story's [ST-xx] ID prefix, regardless of whether the story is actually complete. This is correct for normal autonomous/done stories, but for delegated_backend items where autonomous groundwork is committed with the required [EPIC-xx][ST-xx] prefix (per CLAUDE.md's non-negotiable commit format) while the story itself remains blocked_backend, the issue gets auto-closed prematurely. Issues #1153, #1155, #1156, #1157 were auto-closed this way and had to be manually reopened with a clarifying comment. No clean fix exists within the commit-format rule as written (the ID must appear in the message); the mitigation applied was: always check issue state after any commit that includes a delegated/blocked story's ID, and reopen with a clarifying comment if auto-closed. Worth raising at Phase 3 lessons learnt / post-ship closure as a possible refinement to governance_sync.yml (e.g. only auto-close if the commit message also contains a 'done'/'complete' marker, or if execution_state.json's status for that story is not blocked_*).
